meta.title: The Odyssey: the cineosis sign score
meta.generated_by: tools/forage/product/cineosis.py reads this file; authored against the cineosis table
meta.method: Each scene is read by the table's own test (question), and a sign is kept only when the beat answers it; the neighbour it is most confused with is named with the table's own flip condition and why the scene does not meet it. The primary sign is what the scene is; secondaries are what a shot or a moment in it must do. Variety is not forced: where the film is monotonous that is reported as a finding, and time-images are proposed only where the poem supports them.

direction_contract.shot_bias: weights over WIDE, MID, CLOSE, OBJ (insert) summing to 1: the primary sign's operation at 0.6, secondaries 0.4 between them
direction_contract.hold_min_s: the shortest a shot may be held in this scene (seconds)
direction_contract.move: push | pull | orbit | crane | track | hold (odyssey-trailer.js camAt names)
direction_contract.empty_frame: true: the scene wants at least one shot with no figure (the set's own wide)
direction_contract.sound_forward: true: sound carries the situation; do not cut on lines, drop or hold the bed
direction_contract.cut_rhythm: slow | mid | fast, the keys of odyssey-take.js RHYTHM
direction_contract.insert_object: the thing an OBJ shot is on
direction_contract.subject: whose frame (a halfworld cast id)
direction_contract.book_tempo: the syncwatch's tempo for the book, for comparison
direction_contract.tempo_conflict: the sign's rhythm and the book's are opposite (slow vs fast)

scenes.title: The Gods Consider Odysseus

key_beat.note: she is petitioning Zeus, not commanding him

beats: The Olympian gods assemble while Poseidon is absent among the Ethiopians.
Zeus recalls Aegisthus and argues that mortals enlarge the suffering they blame on gods.
Athena redirects the council toward Odysseus, captive on Calypso's island.
Zeus names Poseidon's anger as the obstacle and permits a plan for Odysseus's return.

primary.name: Milieu
primary.question: What world produces these actions?
primary.answer: The divine order is the situation that produces the whole plot: the council is laid out, and Zeus and Athena speak as instances of it before anyone acts.
primary.operation: Open on an extreme wide of the council hall from high at the back: the ring of gods' thrones small in the frame, then let Zeus and Athena rise inside that order.

avoided.name: Binomial
avoided.flip: It is Binomial instead if the frame is organised by two opposed forces squaring off (two camps, two lines, a standoff) so the setting is only the stage of a duel.
avoided.why_not: Athena petitions, she does not oppose; the frame is a council, not two camps squaring off.

secondary.name: Demark
secondary.question: What breaks the pattern?
secondary.answer: Poseidon's empty seat breaks the ring of occupied thrones; the absence is the fact the scene turns on.
secondary.operation: Hold one wide in which every throne is filled but one; cut to a locked insert of the empty throne with his trident-rest bare.

avoided.name: Mark
avoided.flip: It is a mark instead if the term appears where and as the series predicts.
avoided.why_not: The empty throne is not the next term of a series behaving as predicted; it is the one term out of place.

secondary.name: Icon
secondary.question: Where does intensity become a face?
secondary.answer: Athena's appeal becomes a face held past its information: she petitions, she does not command.
secondary.operation: Push slowly into Athena's head on her key line (appeal) and hold two beats after the line ends.

avoided.name: Bodies of attitude
avoided.flip: It is Body of attitude instead if the close attention falls on the body's postures, fatigue and waiting over duration — a body that carries time — rather than on a face expressing a feeling.
avoided.why_not: What carries the moment is her expression, not a waiting posture carried over time.

scenes.title: Athena's Two-Part Plan

key_beat.note: the decision that starts the poem

beats: Athena proposes sending Hermes to Ogygia with the decree that Calypso release Odysseus.
She assigns herself the journey to Ithaca to awaken courage in Telemachus.
The gods accept the divided operation: release the father and activate the son.
Athena fastens her golden sandals, takes her spear, and leaves Olympus.

primary.name: Vector
primary.question: How do several incomplete situations compose a world?
primary.answer: The plan splits the story into two incomplete missions, Hermes to Ogygia and Athena to Ithaca, that only compose one world when they meet in Book XVI.
primary.operation: Cut between the two errands as she assigns them: Hermes lifting his wand, Athena fastening her sandals; end on a wide in which both leave the hall in different directions.

avoided.name: Index of equivocity
avoided.flip: It is Index of equivocity instead if the film has one principal character facing a two-sided situation rather than a multiplicity of disclosers.
avoided.why_not: There is not one hero facing a two-sided situation; there are two agents on two lines.

secondary.name: Liquid perception
secondary.question: Does perception migrate?
secondary.answer: Perception migrates: the camera leaves Olympus with Athena and hands itself to the palace of Ithaca.
secondary.operation: Crane down with Athena from the hall's edge through cloud to the palace roofs, and land the frame on the stranger's gate, where it picks up the next scene's centre.

avoided.name: Solid perception
avoided.flip: It is Solid instead if, however much the camera travels, it stays locked to one protagonist (a follow-shot behind one walker).
avoided.why_not: The camera does not stay locked to her; she exits frame and the palace takes the centre.

scenes.title: The Stranger at the Threshold

key_beat.note: a boy offering hospitality he cannot afford

beats: Athena arrives at Odysseus's palace disguised as Mentes and waits at the outer gate.
The suitors gamble and feast while servants prepare wine, tables, and meat.
Telemachus notices the unattended stranger and crosses the hall in shame.
He greets her, takes her spear, and leads her away from the suitors' noise.

primary.name: Solid perception
primary.question: Whose world is this?
primary.answer: The world is Telemachus's: he is the one who sees the unattended stranger across a hall that does not see her.
primary.operation: Point of view from Telemachus's seat, past the suitors' shoulders, to the stranger at the gate; reverse on him rising; follow him across the hall and keep him centred.

avoided.name: Liquid perception
avoided.flip: It is Liquid instead if the camera keeps moving and the centre visibly hands off — the figure exits or is overtaken and the frame re-centres on another person, place or event within the shot or cut.
avoided.why_not: The centre does not hand off; the camera returns to Telemachus every time.

secondary.name: Milieu
secondary.question: What world produces these actions?
secondary.answer: The occupied house is the situation that shames him into action: gambling, meat and wine laid out before he moves.
secondary.operation: Open wide on the feast: suitors at the dice, servants carrying tables and meat, the boy small at the far end.

avoided.name: Binomial
avoided.flip: It is Binomial instead if the frame is organised by two opposed forces squaring off (two camps, two lines, a standoff) so the setting is only the stage of a duel.
avoided.why_not: The suitors are shown as a world, not as an opposed camp; no confrontation is staged yet.

scenes.title: Athena Arms Telemachus with a Course

key_beat.note: the goddess drops the disguise's manner

beats: Telemachus explains Penelope's suspended marriage and the suitors' destruction of his estate.
Athena imagines Odysseus returning armed and condemns the suitors' behavior.
She orders Telemachus to call an assembly, dismiss the suitors, and sail for news.
She invokes Orestes as a model and tells Telemachus to leave boyhood behind.

primary.name: Imprint
primary.question: How has the world gotten inside the character?
primary.answer: The occupied house enters Telemachus: Athena loads him with Orestes and an armed father, and the pressure is stored for twenty books.
primary.operation: Hold Telemachus in medium close while Athena speaks; frame the spear she handed him leaning beside him as the object that carries the pressure; no release.

avoided.name: Binomial
avoided.flip: It is Binomial instead if the pressure is externalised as a face-off between two embodied camps, the conflict played out between characters rather than stored inside one.
avoided.why_not: The conflict is placed inside him, not played out as a face-off between the prince and the suitors.

secondary.name: Theatrical figure
secondary.question: What real action is being rehearsed through fiction?
secondary.answer: Orestes and the imagined armed Odysseus are a fiction played over the scene that rehearses the real revenge, which the film defers to Book XXII.
secondary.operation: Stage Athena's imagined Odysseus as a minifigure tableau standing in the doorway in armour, lit apart, while she speaks; it vanishes on the cut back.

avoided.name: Plastic figure
avoided.flip: It is Plastic instead if the figure collapses into one substituted image or cut rather than a sustained performed sequence.
avoided.why_not: It is not one substituted image in one stroke; the Orestes paradigm returns across the film (I, III, XI) as a rehearsed script.

direction.insert_object: the spear Telemachus took from her
direction.subject: telemachus

scenes.title: Hermes Carries the Decree
beats: The gods meet again and Athena presses the case of Odysseus and Telemachus.
Zeus orders Hermes to tell Calypso that Odysseus must depart without divine escort.
Hermes straps on his sandals, takes his wand, and skims across the sea.
He reaches Ogygia, enters Calypso's fragrant cavern, and finds her weaving at the fire.

primary.name: Liquid perception
primary.question: Does perception migrate?
primary.answer: Perception travels with Hermes over the sea and is handed to Calypso at her fire.
primary.operation: Track with Hermes skimming the brick sea, low, then let him fly out of frame as the camera settles on the cave mouth and Calypso weaving inside.

avoided.name: Solid perception
avoided.flip: It is Solid instead if, however much the camera travels, it stays locked to one protagonist (a follow-shot behind one walker).
avoided.why_not: Hermes is not the film's centre; the frame lets him go and re-centres on Ogygia.

secondary.name: Any-space-whatever
secondary.question: Has place stopped functioning as ordinary geography?
secondary.answer: Ogygia is a place outside ordinary geography: grove, springs, birds, no human purpose; the space holds a feeling of suspension.
secondary.operation: Before Hermes enters, hold an empty wide of the grove and the four springs, no figure, for longer than information needs.

avoided.name: Originary world
avoided.flip: It is Originary world instead if the space is a determinate archetypal place — this desert, this forest, the house — charged with primal forces that are about to seize bodies, under a time of decay.
avoided.why_not: Ogygia does not press on bodies with menace or decay; it holds them in suspension.

scenes.title: Odysseus Distrusts Freedom

key_beat.note: do not be angry — he is asking a goddess for release

beats: Calypso finds Odysseus weeping on the shore and tells him to build a raft for home.
He suspects a trap and demands a binding oath that she will not plan his ruin.
Calypso swears by earth, sky, and Styx and offers practical help.
At supper she argues that immortality with her surpasses Penelope; Odysseus tactfully refuses the comparison's consequence.

primary.name: Bodies of attitude
primary.question: What does the body think before it acts?
primary.answer: The body thinks before it acts: Odysseus on the shore, weeping at the sea day after day, is posture with no act prepared.
primary.operation: Hold a static wide of Odysseus seated on the rock, back to us, head bowed toward the horizon, for eight seconds before Calypso enters the frame.

avoided.name: Figure of enfeeblement
avoided.flip: It is enfeeblement instead if the lassitude is the waning of a character's ability to act, measured against actions still expected.
avoided.why_not: His stillness is not measured against an action the film expects of him; it is seven years of waiting as the image.

secondary.name: Any-space-whatever
secondary.question: Has place stopped functioning as ordinary geography?
secondary.answer: The empty sea horizon he stares at is a space charging his longing; the film returns to action with the oath and the raft.
secondary.operation: Reverse from behind him: two-thirds of the frame empty sea and haze, no ship.

avoided.name: Opsign
avoided.flip: It is an opsign instead if the space is freed from any sensory-motor linkage — no character will act on it, nothing it expresses feeds a next action — and is simply seen, with the seer stranded before it.
avoided.why_not: The sea is not a sight that stalls the film for good; the next beat (the oath) turns it into action.

secondary.name: Icon
secondary.question: Where does intensity become a face?
secondary.answer: His appeal to a goddess is a face: 'do not be angry'.
secondary.operation: Close on Odysseus as he asks for the oath, held through Calypso's reply.

avoided.name: Bodies of attitude
avoided.flip: It is Body of attitude instead if the close attention falls on the body's postures, fatigue and waiting over duration — a body that carries time — rather than on a face expressing a feeling.
avoided.why_not: The close-up carries an expression, a petition, not the body's fatigue.

scenes.title: Telemachus Calls the Assembly

key_beat.note: he claims the assembly in front of men who dismiss him

beats: At dawn Telemachus dresses, arms himself, and orders heralds to summon Ithaca.
He enters the meeting ground with two hounds and takes Odysseus's old seat.
Aegyptius asks who has called the first assembly since the fleet sailed for Troy.
Telemachus rises with the speaker's staff and names the double ruin of his father and his house.

primary.name: Milieu
primary.question: What world produces these actions?
primary.answer: Ithaca's assembly, the first since the fleet left, is the social world that must produce an answer to the suitors.
primary.operation: Open extreme wide on the stone meeting ground at dawn, elders on benches, the people ringed; Telemachus enters small with his two hounds.

avoided.name: Quotidian
avoided.flip: It is Quotidian instead if the everyday life shown is a reflection-image that turns the large form around — ordinary, un-heroic banality that deflates or inverts the action form.
avoided.why_not: The assembly is not ordinary banality turned critical; it is the determining social space the large form begins from.

secondary.name: Symbol
secondary.question: What idea is being thought through this thing?
secondary.answer: The speaker's staff and Odysseus's empty seat hold the idea of kingship that every relation in the scene passes through.
secondary.operation: Insert the staff as the herald places it in Telemachus's hand; hold a low frame on the seat before he sits in it.

avoided.name: Fetish
avoided.flip: It is a fetish instead if the object is invested with drive (grabbed, hoarded, torn at, possessed) in an originary world of impulse.
avoided.why_not: The staff is not grabbed as a thing of primal force; it carries a right to speak.

scenes.title: The Secret of Penelope's Loom
beats: Antinous rejects Telemachus's charge and blames Penelope for prolonging the courtship.
He recounts how she wove Laertes's shroud by day and secretly unraveled it by night.
A maid exposed the deception and the suitors forced Penelope to finish the web.
Antinous demands that Telemachus send his mother back to Icarius to choose a husband.

primary.name: Mark
primary.question: What recurring thing has become meaningful because it repeats?
primary.answer: Weaving by day and unweaving by night, three years running, is a habitual series whose meaning is the stratagem.
primary.operation: Three matched overhead frames of the loom in the same composition: web full in daylight, web unpicked under a torch, web full again; the same lens, the same cut rhythm.

avoided.name: Demark
avoided.flip: It is a demark instead if the shot shows one instance that breaks the established series: wrong place, wrong form, wrong time.
avoided.why_not: The series is shown while it holds; its break (the maid) is a second sign, not this one.

secondary.name: Demark
secondary.question: What breaks the pattern?
secondary.answer: The maid who betrays the secret is the term that breaks the series.
secondary.operation: Fourth frame of the loom series: the same overhead framing, now with the maid's figure in the doorway where no one should be.

avoided.name: Index of equivocity
avoided.flip: It is an index of equivocity instead if the shot presents one action that can be read two ways, with no prior habitual series being broken.
avoided.why_not: The betrayal is not one act read two ways; it is an aberration in an established series.

secondary.name: Binomial
secondary.question: Where has the world become a duel?
secondary.answer: Antinous and Telemachus square off across the assembly; the image is a duel of speeches.
secondary.operation: Shot and reverse shot on a single axis between Antinous standing and Telemachus with the staff, the crowd split behind each.

avoided.name: Milieu
avoided.flip: It is Milieu instead if the figures are present only as instances of their world, with no opposition structuring the frame.
avoided.why_not: The two men are not just instances of Ithaca; the frame is organised by their opposition.

scenes.title: The Night Launch
beats: Athena, disguised as Telemachus, recruits crewmen and borrows Noemon's ship.
She casts drowsiness over the suitors and calls the prince outside.
The crew carries provisions from the palace and stows them below deck.
Telemachus boards; Athena takes the pilot's seat and sends a strong west wind.
The sail fills, libations are poured, and the ship travels through the night.

primary.name: Liquid perception
primary.question: Does perception migrate?
primary.answer: Perception passes hand to hand, from the storeroom jars to the crew to the ship and its filling sail.
primary.operation: One travelling shot along the line of men carrying jars down to the black ship; the camera leaves each carrier as the next takes the jar, and rises to the sail as it fills.

avoided.name: Dividual
avoided.flip: It is Dividual instead if the travelling camera over many people is expressing one shared affect of the mass — panic, joy, grief — rather than passing attention from centre to centre.
avoided.why_not: The crew is not expressing one shared feeling; attention passes from centre to centre.

secondary.name: Any-space-whatever
secondary.question: Has place stopped functioning as ordinary geography?
secondary.answer: The night sea with a single torch on deck is a space that carries the feeling of the voyage (the trailer's frame 47: how small a light is at sea).
secondary.operation: Wide, blue-black sea tiles to the horizon, the ship a dark mass, one warm point of fire; hold it.

avoided.name: Opsign
avoided.flip: It is an opsign instead if the space is freed from any sensory-motor linkage — no character will act on it, nothing it expresses feeds a next action — and is simply seen, with the seer stranded before it.
avoided.why_not: The film goes straight back into action (Pylos at dawn); the night sea charges the voyage, it does not stall the film.

scenes.title: Telemachus Questions Nestor

key_beat.note: you bring it all back

beats: After the meal Nestor asks the strangers who they are and whether they are traders or raiders.
Telemachus identifies himself and asks for the unsoftened truth about Odysseus.
Nestor remembers Troy and praises Odysseus's unequalled cunning.
He begins the account of the quarrel that split the returning Greek fleet.

primary.name: Weak destiny
primary.question: Does memory color the present without dictating it?
primary.answer: Nestor's memory of Troy colours the present without dictating it: he remembers, praises, and has no news to give.
primary.operation: Hold Nestor and Telemachus by the sacrificial fire at dusk; no marked flashback, the Troy memory as sound and a glance toward the sea.

avoided.name: Strong destiny
avoided.flip: It is Strong destiny instead if the flashback is clearly marked and complete and directly produces an action.
avoided.why_not: No marked flashback returns to drive an act; the recollection ends in 'I do not know'.

secondary.name: Icon
secondary.question: Where does intensity become a face?
secondary.answer: Nestor's face is where the grief of Troy becomes visible ('you bring it all back').
secondary.operation: Close on Nestor's face held after his line; the fire's flicker on it.

avoided.name: Dividual
avoided.flip: It is Dividual instead if the face is one of a series of faces or bodies that together express one collective emotion, the individual standing in for the mass.
avoided.why_not: It is one old man's grief, not the feeling of a crowd.

secondary.name: Milieu
secondary.question: What world produces these actions?
secondary.answer: Pylos, a pious ordered kingdom (nine companies sacrificing to Poseidon), is the milieu the son is measured against.
secondary.operation: Open wide on the beach with the nine divisions and the altar fires before the conversation.

avoided.name: Originary world
avoided.flip: It is Originary world instead if the place is timeless and primal — an archetypal forest or house rumbling with drives and entropy — rather than historically and socially dated.
avoided.why_not: The beach is historical and social (the kingdom at sacrifice), not a timeless primal ground.

scenes.title: Athena Reveals Herself at Pylos

key_beat.note: dear boy, no fear that you prove base

beats: Night approaches and Nestor invites the guests to his palace.
Athena refuses and suddenly flies away in the form of a sea-eagle.
Nestor recognizes divine favor and prays to Athena.
At dawn a heifer is sacrificed; Telemachus is bathed and dressed for departure.

primary.name: Limpid and opaque
primary.question: Which side of the image is becoming real?
primary.answer: One face of the image clears as the other clouds: Mentor goes opaque and the sea-eagle becomes the true image of the goddess.
primary.operation: Wide on the courtyard at dusk: Mentor's figure is replaced, on twos, by the eagle rising from the same mark; hold on the empty mark after.

avoided.name: Mirrors face to face
avoided.flip: It is mirrors face to face instead if the doubles are all present at once and nothing passes from clear to opaque.
avoided.why_not: There are not several reflections at once; one face passes into the other.

secondary.name: Icon
secondary.question: Where does intensity become a face?
secondary.answer: Nestor's awe is a face: the old king sees a god left his table.
secondary.operation: Close on Nestor looking up, the eagle out of frame.

avoided.name: Symptom
avoided.flip: It is Symptom instead if the facial intensity has already tipped into a primordial act — gnawing, biting, lunging, grabbing — the face as the site of an impulse too strong for the character.
avoided.why_not: His intensity does not tip into an act; he prays, he does not seize.

scenes.title: Recognition through Tears

key_beat.note: never have I seen such likeness — the poem's first

beats: Menelaus speaks of Odysseus and Telemachus hides his tears behind his cloak.
Helen enters, recognizes Telemachus by resemblance, and names him aloud.
Pisistratus confirms the identity and recalls his own dead brother Antilochus.
All four weep until Menelaus calls for the mourning to end with the meal.

primary.name: Icon
primary.question: Where does intensity become a face?
primary.answer: Helen's recognition becomes a face: 'never have I seen such likeness'. The poem's first recognition is intensity before action.
primary.operation: Push into Helen's face as she looks at Telemachus and hold after she names him.

avoided.name: Dividual
avoided.flip: It is Dividual instead if the face is one of a series of faces or bodies that together express one collective emotion, the individual standing in for the mass.
avoided.why_not: Her recognition is hers, not the room's, until the second sign takes over.

secondary.name: Dividual
secondary.question: Is the feeling mine, ours, or both?
secondary.answer: All four weep: the feeling belongs to the gathering, each one's grief the group's.
secondary.operation: Pan slowly across the four faces at the table, Telemachus's hidden in his cloak, then rest on Menelaus who ends it.

avoided.name: Icon
avoided.flip: It is Icon instead if the camera isolates one face in close-up and the emotion reads as that person's own, not the crowd's reflected in them.
avoided.why_not: No single face carries it; the pan binds four griefs into one.

scenes.title: Helen's Drug and the Beggar in Troy

key_beat.note: she is describing a man who scarred himself to get in

beats: Helen mixes a drug into the wine that quiets grief and anger.
She tells how Odysseus entered Troy disguised as a beaten slave.
Helen alone recognized and bathed him; he revealed the Greek plan after binding her to secrecy.
Odysseus killed Trojans and returned to the ships with intelligence.

primary.name: Theatrical figure
primary.question: What real action is being rehearsed through fiction?
primary.answer: Odysseus disguised as a beaten slave in Troy, bathed and recognised by a woman, is a staged fiction that rehearses the Ithaca plot the film is deferring.
primary.operation: Stage Helen's tale as a tableau in the Troy set: the beggar, the bath, Helen at his feet; frame it exactly as the Eurycleia foot-washing will be framed in XIX.

avoided.name: Plastic figure
avoided.flip: It is Plastic instead if the figure collapses into one substituted image or cut rather than a sustained performed sequence.
avoided.why_not: It is a sequence of performed action, not one substituted image.

secondary.name: Fetish
secondary.question: What object has become charged?
secondary.answer: The mixing bowl holds a drug that quiets grief: a charged object waiting to be drunk.
secondary.operation: Insert of the bowl lit from the lamp as Helen's hand tips the drug in; hold before anyone drinks.

avoided.name: Imprint
avoided.flip: It is Imprint instead if the object is an emotional token of a social situation (a murdered child's keepsake) linking a character's accumulated grievance to a milieu, rather than a vessel of pre-moral primal force.
avoided.why_not: The bowl is not an emotional token of a social situation; its charge is a force (forgetting).

scenes.title: The Wooden Horse
beats: Menelaus answers with the story of the wooden horse.
Helen circled the horse and imitated the voices of the warriors' wives.
The hidden Greeks nearly answered; Odysseus restrained them and silenced Anticlus.
Telemachus hears proof of his father's endurance and command under pressure.

primary.name: Sonsign
primary.image_type: Sonsign / pure actual sound situation (zeroness of the time-image, sound side)
primary.question: Does this sound stand alone as a situation, answered by no action?
primary.answer: Inside the dark horse, the wives' voices hold the situation and must be answered by no action: Odysseus's hand on Anticlus's mouth keeps the sound unanswered.
primary.operation: Black frame inside the horse, faces barely lit, the voices of wives carried off-screen; hold on the frozen listeners; cut to Odysseus's hand over a mouth.

avoided.name: Binomial
avoided.flip: It is an action-image sign (binomial: situation → response) instead if the sound triggers a response: the alarm makes someone run, the phone is answered, the whistle ends the shift.
avoided.why_not: The sound does not trigger a response; the scene is built on the response being stopped.

secondary.name: Powers of the false
secondary.question: What if contradiction generates rather than obstructs the story?
secondary.answer: Helen's imitation of the wives' voices contradicts Helen's own story a scene earlier; no version is ranked as the true Helen.
secondary.operation: Cut from the voices to Helen outside circling the horse, lit from below, her mouth making another woman's voice; do not mark which of the two tales is true.

avoided.name: Limpid and opaque
avoided.flip: It is limpid and opaque instead if the exchange is local to one image (the glass, the role) and the narration's truth is not at stake.
avoided.why_not: The truth of the whole telling is at stake (whose Helen?), not one image's two faces.

scenes.title: Menelaus Wrestles Proteus
beats: Telemachus asks directly for news of Odysseus.
Menelaus recounts being trapped in Egypt until Eidothea taught him to seize Proteus.
He and three men hid beneath sealskins and grappled the Old Man of the Sea.
Proteus changed into beasts, water, and a tree before yielding prophecy.
He revealed that Odysseus lived, detained by Calypso on an island.

primary.name: Index of lack
primary.question: What missing situation does this action let us infer?
primary.answer: The grappling is the action that fills the ellipsis in one disclosure: Proteus yields that Odysseus lives, held by Calypso.
primary.operation: Build from the ambush to Proteus's surrender; land on one image as he speaks: a small insert of Odysseus on Calypso's shore (the frame from V-S03).

avoided.name: Index of equivocity
avoided.flip: It is Index of equivocity instead if the disclosure splits — the same act or clue points to two distant situations and the film refuses to settle which.
avoided.why_not: The disclosure is unequivocal and redirects Telemachus homeward; nothing stays double.

secondary.name: Symptom
secondary.question: What force is acting through this body?
secondary.answer: Men under sealskins grappling the Old Man behave as animals: the act before thought.
secondary.operation: Handheld close on the pile of bodies under stinking skins, 12 fps pose-to-pose grapple.

avoided.name: Imprint
avoided.flip: It is Imprint instead if the violent act is the release of pressure slowly accumulated from a complex social situation, legible through a long build and an emotional object.
avoided.why_not: No social pressure has built up; it is a raw physical struggle.

secondary.name: Gaseous perception
secondary.question: Can the world perceive without a human center?
secondary.answer: Proteus's changes into lion, snake, water and tree give an image in which no form is privileged.
secondary.operation: Replacement animation on twos: the figure swapped for brick lion, snake, a column of clear plates, a tree, each held two frames, the men's hands constant.

avoided.name: Liquid perception
avoided.flip: It is Liquid instead if, despite the flow, the image settles for a moment on a character or event we are invited to follow.
avoided.why_not: The image does not settle on a character to follow; it is matter in variation.

scenes.title: The Suitors Prepare an Ambush
beats: In Ithaca, Noemon asks Antinous when Telemachus will return his ship.
The suitors discover that the voyage truly occurred without their knowledge.
Antinous selects a crew and sails to the strait between Ithaca and Same to ambush the prince.
Medon overhears and tells Penelope; she collapses in fear.
Athena sends a phantom in the shape of Iphthime to reassure the sleeping queen.

primary.name: Vector
primary.question: How do several incomplete situations compose a world?
primary.answer: Several incomplete situations compose one world: the discovered voyage, the ambush crew, Medon overhearing, Penelope collapsing, the phantom.
primary.operation: Cross-cut the threads, each in its own framing: the ambush ship pushing off, Medon at the door, Penelope on the floor; each leaves a gap the next fills.

avoided.name: Liquid perception
avoided.flip: It is Liquid perception instead if the ensemble is only a flow of perceived centres with no situation being disclosed by their actions.
avoided.why_not: The ensemble discloses situations, not merely a flow of perceived centres.

secondary.name: Rich dream
secondary.question: Can we clearly tell when the dream begins?
secondary.answer: Iphthime's phantom entering the sleeping queen's room is marked as dream.
secondary.operation: Dissolve on Penelope asleep; the phantom arrives as a double exposure standing by the bed; dissolve out.

avoided.name: Restrained dream
avoided.flip: It is Restrained instead if entry is a straight cut and the dream looks like concrete everyday reality with only an uncanny slip.
avoided.why_not: The entry is marked and ornate, not an invisible cut.

scenes.title: Building the Raft
beats: Calypso leads Odysseus to tall trees and gives him axe, adze, augers, cloth, and cord.
He fells, trims, bores, joins, decks, and fences the timbers over four days.
He rigs mast, yard, sail, steering oar, and ballast.
Calypso bathes and clothes him, loads food and water, and sends a warm wind behind the raft.

primary.name: Quotidian
primary.question: Has everyday life become both ridiculous and heroic?
primary.answer: Carpentry for four days is both an ordinary craft and the heroic act of leaving a goddess; the scene cannot decide which.
primary.operation: Static medium shots of each task (fell, trim, bore, join, deck, rig), held long, no music swell.

avoided.name: Figure of enfeeblement
avoided.flip: It is Enfeeblement instead if the act reads plainly as futile and the world plainly as overwhelming.
avoided.why_not: His acts are effective and dignified; the world does not swell over a futile figure.

secondary.name: Mark
secondary.question: What recurring thing has become meaningful because it repeats?
secondary.answer: Four days are four terms of a series: the raft grows one course per matched frame.
secondary.operation: Four matched top-down frames of the raft on the same grid, a stage of the build added each time, like instruction-booklet steps.

avoided.name: Sheets of the past
avoided.flip: It is sheets of the past instead if the recurring image returns the viewer to different, non-chronological layers of the past rather than building a logical inference.
avoided.why_not: The repetitions build an inference forward, not a return to layers of the past.

scenes.title: Poseidon Breaks the Sea
beats: For seventeen days Odysseus steers by the stars until Scheria rises ahead.
Poseidon sees him, gathers clouds, and strikes the sea with a four-wind storm.
The raft rolls; Odysseus is swept away and barely regains it.
Ino gives him an immortal veil and orders him to abandon the raft and swim.
Athena restrains the winds except the north wind that drives him shoreward.

primary.name: Originary world
primary.question: What ancient or pre-social force underlies this milieu?
primary.answer: The sea under Poseidon's four winds is an ancient force that seizes the body and the raft.
primary.operation: Wide, black sky and a heaving brick sea, the raft small; low camera at water level when the wave rolls it.

avoided.name: Any-space-whatever
avoided.flip: It is Any-space-whatever instead if the space is indeterminate — a void, a fog, a colour field — expressing a pure affective quality with no specific primal place and no pressure on bodies.
avoided.why_not: The storm is a determinate primal place pressing on a body, not a void of pure affect.

secondary.name: Binomial
secondary.question: Where has the world become a duel?
secondary.answer: Poseidon sees him: the god and the man are the two lines of force of the whole voyage.
secondary.operation: Cut from Poseidon on the headland looking out to the raft and back on one axis; the next wave is his reply.

avoided.name: Milieu
avoided.flip: It is Milieu instead if the figures are present only as instances of their world, with no opposition structuring the frame.
avoided.why_not: This is not a milieu shot; the frame is organised by the god's opposition.

secondary.name: Fetish
secondary.question: What object has become charged?
secondary.answer: Ino's veil is the charged object that keeps him alive.
secondary.operation: Insert of the veil in his fist under water, white against the dark tiles.

avoided.name: Mark
avoided.flip: It is Mark instead if the object's charge comes from habitual relation — it belongs to a familiar series (a cigarette case, a set of keys) and its meaning emerges when that series is recognised or broken.
avoided.why_not: The veil is not one term of a habitual series; it carries a force of its own.

scenes.title: The River Accepts the Castaway

key_beat.note: I come to your current a suppliant

beats: Odysseus swims for two nights and days while waves hurl him toward a reef-lined coast.
Athena shows him a river mouth free of rocks and wind.
He prays to the river god, who stills the current and receives him.
Odysseus returns Ino's veil to the sea, crawls ashore, and hides beneath two intertwined olive bushes.
He buries himself in leaves and Athena seals him in sleep.

primary.name: Figure of enfeeblement
primary.question: Is the actor tiny compared with the world disclosed?
primary.answer: A tiny swimmer against a reef coast: his small acts make the immense sea swell into view.
primary.operation: Extreme wide from the cliffs: the head a few pixels among the surf lines, the reef white; pull back.

avoided.name: Quotidian
avoided.flip: It is Quotidian instead if the small acts are neither futile nor merely revelatory but carry their own petty heroism, so trivial and immense can't be separated.
avoided.why_not: His acts are not a petty daily heroism; they are the survival of a speck against the sea.

secondary.name: Bodies of attitude
secondary.question: What does the body think before it acts?
secondary.answer: The body buried in leaves and sealed in sleep is posture with no act prepared.
secondary.operation: Top shot on the leaf pile under the two olives, the body inside, held long; only the light changes.

avoided.name: Bodies of gest
avoided.flip: It is a body of gest instead if attitudes are linked into a performed social gesture addressed or staged (Brechtian demonstration, ritual, choreographed routine).
avoided.why_not: No gesture performs a social act; he simply sleeps.

secondary.name: Icon
secondary.question: Where does intensity become a face?
secondary.answer: His appeal to the river is a face.
secondary.operation: Close on Odysseus in the river mouth as he prays, water to the chin.

avoided.name: Symptom
avoided.flip: It is Symptom instead if the facial intensity has already tipped into a primordial act — gnawing, biting, lunging, grabbing — the face as the site of an impulse too strong for the character.
avoided.why_not: The face appeals; the body does not lunge or grab.

scenes.title: Athena Enters Nausicaa's Dream
beats: Athena reaches the palace of Alcinous and enters Nausicaa's chamber in the likeness of a friend.
She reproaches the princess for leaving fine clothes unwashed before marriage.
Nausicaa wakes, asks her father for a wagon, and conceals the marriage motive.
Alcinous orders the mule cart prepared; her mother packs food, wine, and oil.

primary.name: Restrained dream
primary.question: Are we unsure whether waking has ended?
primary.answer: Nausicaa's dream is an ordinary chat about laundry with a friend; only its visitor is impossible, so we cannot be sure she was awake.
primary.operation: No dissolve: straight cut from the sleeping princess to the friend at the bedside talking; the friend is simply there.

avoided.name: Rich dream
avoided.flip: It is Rich instead if the entry is ornate and the imagery overtly strange.
avoided.why_not: The entry is not marked or ornate; the dream is made of everyday things.

secondary.name: Quotidian
secondary.question: Has everyday life become both ridiculous and heroic?
secondary.answer: The laundry wagon, the mother's packing: domestic banality that secretly prepares a marriage and a rescue.
secondary.operation: Static medium shots on the mule cart being loaded, the food and oil.

avoided.name: Figure of enfeeblement
avoided.flip: It is Enfeeblement instead if the act reads plainly as futile and the world plainly as overwhelming.
avoided.why_not: Nothing here is futile; it is ordinary and consequential at once.

scenes.title: Laundry and Ball at the River
beats: Nausicaa and her maids drive to the washing pools, unharness the mules, and tread the clothes clean.
They spread garments on the shore, bathe, eat, and play ball while the clothes dry.
Athena deflects the ball into deep water; the girls cry out.
The shout wakes Odysseus beneath the leaves.

primary.name: Quotidian
primary.question: Has everyday life become both ridiculous and heroic?
primary.answer: Washing and play by the river are the ordinary life of girls, both trivial and the hinge of the hero's fate.
primary.operation: Hold static mediums on treading the clothes in the pools; then the ball game.

avoided.name: Opsign
avoided.flip: It is an Opsign instead if the everyday is shown as a pure optical situation where no one can act at all (Ozu's empty vase, still lifes) rather than as an act of duty.
avoided.why_not: Action is not suspended; the girls wash, play and shout.

secondary.name: Vector
secondary.question: How do several incomplete situations compose a world?
secondary.answer: Two independent lines share one frame: the girls' game and the sleeper under the leaves; the ball crosses from one into the other.
secondary.operation: Wide with the girls playing in the foreground and the leaf pile in the corner; the ball flies into the deep pool and the cry reaches the sleeper.

avoided.name: Liquid perception
avoided.flip: It is Liquid perception instead if the ensemble is only a flow of perceived centres with no situation being disclosed by their actions.
avoided.why_not: The ball's flight discloses a situation (a man is here), not only a moving centre.

scenes.title: The Naked Stranger Emerges

key_beat.note: the kindest greeting a stranger gets in the poem

beats: Odysseus debates whether to clasp Nausicaa's knees or speak from a distance.
Covering himself with a leafy branch, he emerges like a mountain lion.
The maids flee, but Athena keeps Nausicaa steady.
Odysseus praises her tactfully, asks for clothing and directions, and avoids touching her.
Nausicaa answers with courage and assigns the maids to help him.

primary.name: Binomial
primary.question: Where has the world become a duel?
primary.answer: The shore becomes a duel, romantic and dangerous: the lion-like naked man and the princess who stands her ground.
primary.operation: Wide on one axis: Odysseus emerging with the branch at one side, Nausicaa alone at the other, maids scattering between; then shot/reverse at a distance neither closes.

avoided.name: Milieu
avoided.flip: It is Milieu instead if the figures are present only as instances of their world, with no opposition structuring the frame.
avoided.why_not: They are not just instances of Phaeacia; the frame is organised by the two of them facing.

secondary.name: Index of equivocity
secondary.question: What two worlds could explain the same action?
secondary.answer: His emergence reads two ways, a predator (the lion simile) and a suppliant; the maids read one, Nausicaa the other.
secondary.operation: Frame his emergence once from the fleeing maids' side (lion) and once from Nausicaa's (suppliant) without resolving until he speaks.

avoided.name: Index of lack
avoided.flip: It is Index of lack instead if a later action resolves which situation is true and the character reorients on that single reading.
avoided.why_not: The film holds the doubleness for the emergence; only his first words settle it, which is why this is secondary.

scenes.title: Athena Hides the Walk through Scheria

key_beat.note: they do not warm to strangers

beats: Nausicaa reaches the palace while Odysseus waits in Athena's grove.
He enters the city wrapped in a divine mist.
Athena appears as a young girl carrying a pitcher and guides him through streets and harbor.
She describes the Phaeacians, warns him not to question passersby, and directs him to Arete.

primary.name: Liquid perception
primary.question: Does perception migrate?
primary.answer: Perception migrates through Scheria: the camera walks with the pair and hands itself to the harbours, the ships and the walls as the girl names them.
primary.operation: Track beside Odysseus and the pitcher girl through streets; let passers-by cross in front and let the camera drift to the harbour and the long walls.

avoided.name: Solid perception
avoided.flip: It is Solid instead if, however much the camera travels, it stays locked to one protagonist (a follow-shot behind one walker).
avoided.why_not: The camera does not stay locked to Odysseus; the city takes the centre.

secondary.name: Limpid and opaque
secondary.question: Which side of the image is becoming real?
secondary.answer: Wrapped in mist, Odysseus is the opaque side of the image: the city looks through him.
secondary.operation: Figures pass in front of him without looking; grade him slightly veiled (a clear-plate layer, fog near him only).

avoided.name: Mirrors face to face
avoided.flip: It is mirrors face to face instead if the doubles are all present at once and nothing passes from clear to opaque.
avoided.why_not: He is not doubled in reflections; he is half there.

scenes.title: The Palace and the Gardens
beats: Odysseus stops before Alcinous's palace, dazzled by bronze walls, golden doors, and guardian dogs.
He observes the fifty women weaving and grinding within.
Outside, an orchard and garden bear fruit through every season.
He crosses the threshold under mist and finds the royal feast in progress.

primary.name: Milieu
primary.question: What world produces these actions?
primary.answer: The Phaeacian order (bronze walls, golden doors, fifty women at looms and mills) is laid out before anyone acts inside it.
primary.operation: Extreme wide of the palace front with Odysseus small at the threshold; then wides of the women at work.

avoided.name: Originary world
avoided.flip: It is Originary world instead if the place is timeless and primal — an archetypal forest or house rumbling with drives and entropy — rather than historically and socially dated.
avoided.why_not: The palace is a social and historical order, not a timeless primal ground.

secondary.name: Peaks of the present
secondary.question: What if several presents are simultaneously valid?
secondary.answer: The orchard bears blossom, green fruit and ripe fruit on the same branch: several presents of one tree at once.
secondary.operation: Insert of one branch built with round plates in three colours (flower, green, ripe) in one frame; hold.

avoided.name: Sheets of the past
avoided.flip: It is sheets of the past instead if the coexistence is of strata of the past explored as a memory-world, not of presents.
avoided.why_not: These are nows side by side, not strata of the past.

direction.insert_object: a branch in flower, green and ripe at once
direction.subject: odysseus

scenes.title: Supplication at Arete's Knees

key_beat.note: at the queen's knees, formally

beats: Athena's mist falls away only when Odysseus reaches Arete.
He clasps her knees and asks passage home, then sits humbly in the ashes by the hearth.
The hall remains silent until the elder Echeneus tells Alcinous to raise the suppliant.
Odysseus is seated beside the king, fed, and promised a convoy home.

primary.name: Bodies of gest
primary.question: How do postures become social relations?
primary.answer: The supplication (clasping the queen's knees, sitting in the ashes) is a posture chained into a ritual gesture, and the silent hall watches it as ceremony.
primary.operation: Frontal wide of the hearth: Odysseus at Arete's knees, then seated in the ashes; the hall frozen; hold until Echeneus speaks.

avoided.name: Bodies of attitude
avoided.flip: It is a body of attitude instead if the body stays in one posture with no linkage into a performed act.
avoided.why_not: The body does not remain in one posture; it performs a social act.

secondary.name: Limpid and opaque
secondary.question: Which side of the image is becoming real?
secondary.answer: The mist falls away as he touches her knees: the stranger clears.
secondary.operation: The veil layer on Odysseus lifts over two seconds as his hands reach Arete.

avoided.name: Rich dream
avoided.flip: It is a rich dream instead if the obscure side is marked as a character's dream with a clear waking frame around it.
avoided.why_not: No dreamer frames it; it is the image itself clearing.

scenes.title: Arete Recognizes Her Work

key_beat.note: hard to tell all my griefs

beats: After the Phaeacians leave, Arete recognizes the clothes Odysseus wears as garments from her household.
She asks who he is and how he obtained them.
Odysseus tells of Calypso, the storm, Nausicaa, and his choice not to follow the princess directly.
Alcinous praises his restraint, offers marriage, and renews the promise of safe passage at dawn.

primary.name: Demark
primary.question: What breaks the pattern?
primary.answer: Arete's own weaving appears where it cannot belong, on a stranger's back; the aberration makes her think.
primary.operation: Insert of the cloak's pattern, then Arete's look from it to his face; the cloak framed beside her own maids' work.

avoided.name: Mark
avoided.flip: It is a mark instead if the term appears where and as the series predicts.
avoided.why_not: The cloak is not a term where the series predicts it; it is her household's cloth out of place.

secondary.name: Weak destiny
secondary.question: Does memory color the present without dictating it?
secondary.answer: His account of Calypso and the storm is memory colouring the present (weariness) without directing an act.
secondary.operation: No flashback marker: a slow push on Odysseus as he tells it; the storm only in the firelight and the sound.

avoided.name: Strong destiny
avoided.flip: It is Strong destiny instead if the flashback is clearly marked and complete and directly produces an action.
avoided.why_not: The told past does not close a circuit into action; Alcinous acts, not the teller.

scenes.note: Index of lack is the first reading and the table flips it: the disclosure comes from a household series broken, so Demark.

scenes.title: The Phaeacian Assembly and the Ship

key_beat.note: a king ordering a ship down to the sea

beats: At dawn Athena moves through the city in a herald's form, calling the people to assembly.
She makes Odysseus appear larger and more impressive as he enters.
Alcinous orders fifty-two sailors to prepare a ship and invites the nobles to feast.
The people ready the vessel while the palace fills for celebration.

primary.name: Milieu
primary.question: What world produces these actions?
primary.answer: Phaeacia at assembly, a seafaring people readying a ship, is the world that will carry him home.
primary.operation: Wide on the assembly ground and the harbour: fifty-two sailors hauling the ship down.

avoided.name: Binomial
avoided.flip: It is Binomial instead if the frame is organised by two opposed forces squaring off (two camps, two lines, a standoff) so the setting is only the stage of a duel.
avoided.why_not: No two sides face off; the whole city works one task.

secondary.name: Liquid perception
secondary.question: Does perception migrate?
secondary.answer: Athena as herald moves through the town and the camera goes with her from door to door until the crowd takes the frame.
secondary.operation: Follow the herald through the streets, handing the shot to the gathering people.

avoided.name: Dividual
avoided.flip: It is Dividual instead if the travelling camera over many people is expressing one shared affect of the mass — panic, joy, grief — rather than passing attention from centre to centre.
avoided.why_not: The crowd is not expressing one feeling; attention passes on.

scenes.title: The Trojan Horse Song and the Name

key_beat.note: he has noticed his guest weeping

beats: Odysseus gives Demodocus a choice cut of meat and asks for the song of the wooden horse.
The bard sings the Greeks' emergence, the sack, and Odysseus's attack on Deiphobus's house.
Odysseus weeps like a captive woman over a fallen husband.
Alcinous stops the music and asks the stranger for his name, homeland, and reason for grief.
Odysseus prepares to narrate his wanderings.

primary.name: Mise en abyme
primary.question: Is one action-world nested inside another?
primary.answer: The bard sings Odysseus's own deeds to Odysseus: one action-world nested inside another, the hero watching himself as a character.
primary.operation: Frame the singer with a tableau of the horse behind him in the lamplight while Odysseus listens in the foreground; the told Troy and the listening hall share the image.

avoided.name: Theatrical figure
avoided.flip: It is Theatrical instead if the nested performance has a clear outside: one real action that the play-within points toward.
avoided.why_not: The nested performance has no single outside it points to; it folds the hero into his own story.

secondary.name: Sonsign
secondary.image_type: Sonsign / pure actual sound situation (zeroness of the time-image, sound side)
secondary.question: Does this sound stand alone as a situation, answered by no action?
secondary.answer: The lyre and the song hold the hall; the listener cannot act, only weep under his cloak.
secondary.operation: Hold on the hall with the song carrying it; do not cut on the lyrics.

avoided.name: Binomial
avoided.flip: It is an action-image sign (binomial: situation → response) instead if the sound triggers a response: the alarm makes someone run, the phone is answered, the whistle ends the shift.
avoided.why_not: The song triggers no response; Alcinous stops it because of the tears, not because the song called for action.

secondary.name: Icon
secondary.question: Where does intensity become a face?
secondary.answer: His weeping, face veiled by the purple cloak, is intensity with no outlet.
secondary.operation: Close on the cloak drawn over his head, one eye visible, held.

avoided.name: Bodies of attitude
avoided.flip: It is Body of attitude instead if the close attention falls on the body's postures, fatigue and waiting over duration — a body that carries time — rather than on a face expressing a feeling.
avoided.why_not: It is a face, not a tired posture.

scenes.title: Odysseus Names Himself

key_beat.note: the compliment that opens four books of lies

beats: Odysseus praises Demodocus and the ordered feast.
He finally declares his name, lineage, and Ithacan homeland.
He describes Ithaca's rugged beauty and his longing to return.
He begins the account of the disasters that followed Troy.

primary.name: Mise en abyme
primary.question: Is one action-world nested inside another?
primary.answer: The tale is about to nest inside the feast: the hero names himself and the next four books are told inside this hall.
primary.operation: Open on the hall with Odysseus standing; pull back until the listeners fill the foreground and a tableau of Ithaca rises behind him; the tale begins inside that frame.

avoided.name: Theatrical figure
avoided.flip: It is Theatrical instead if the nested performance has a clear outside: one real action that the play-within points toward.
avoided.why_not: The nested tale has no single real action it rehearses.

secondary.name: Powers of the false
secondary.question: What if contradiction generates rather than obstructs the story?
secondary.answer: The compliment that opens four books of lies: the teller is the poem's great liar, and nothing can check him.
secondary.operation: Hold the Phaeacian faces, not his, as he says his name; the frame is on the audience who must believe.

avoided.name: Limpid and opaque
avoided.flip: It is limpid and opaque instead if the exchange is local to one image (the glass, the role) and the narration's truth is not at stake.
avoided.why_not: What is at stake is the truth of the whole telling, not one image's two faces.

secondary.name: Solid perception
secondary.question: Whose world is this?
secondary.answer: From here, every image of the tales is Odysseus's world.
secondary.operation: Centre Odysseus dead in the frame as he names himself, the hall arranged round him.

avoided.name: Icon
avoided.flip: It is Icon instead if the frame is a close-up in which the face itself is the whole image — expression cut off from space and motor outlet — rather than a person positioned as the axis of a surrounding world.
avoided.why_not: He is placed as the axis of a world, not a face alone.

scenes.title: The Raid on the Cicones
beats: Odysseus's fleet sacks Ismarus and divides the captured wealth.
He orders immediate departure, but the crews remain to feast on sheep, cattle, and wine.
Cicones from inland arrive in organized force and fight through the day.
Six men from every ship are killed before the fleet escapes at dusk.

primary.name: Binomial
primary.question: Where has the world become a duel?
primary.answer: Two armies square off all day: the fleet against the Cicones.
primary.operation: Wide on the beach with the two lines opposed; cut in on single clashes along the axis; end with the fleet's line breaking at dusk.

avoided.name: Milieu
avoided.flip: It is Milieu instead if the figures are present only as instances of their world, with no opposition structuring the frame.
avoided.why_not: The town is only the stage; the frame is a battle line.

secondary.name: Symptom
secondary.question: What force is acting through this body?
secondary.answer: The crews feast on sheep and wine against orders: appetite before thought, and it costs six men from every ship.
secondary.operation: Close shots of eating and drinking at the fires while Odysseus's order goes unheeded.

avoided.name: Imprint
avoided.flip: It is Imprint instead if the violent act is the release of pressure slowly accumulated from a complex social situation, legible through a long build and an emotional object.
avoided.why_not: The appetite is immediate, no accumulated social situation behind it.

scenes.title: The Lotus-Eaters

key_beat.note: bind them under the benches

beats: A north wind drives the ships off course for nine days.
They land among the Lotus-eaters and send three scouts inland.
The inhabitants offer lotus; those who taste it lose all desire for home.
Odysseus drags the weeping men back, binds them under the benches, and orders immediate departure.

primary.name: Bodies of attitude
primary.question: What does the body think before it acts?
primary.answer: The lotus-eaters and the men who taste the fruit are bodies with no wish to act: posture as content.
primary.operation: Hold a static wide of bodies lying in the meadow, the scouts among them; no movement but breath.

avoided.name: Figure of enfeeblement
avoided.flip: It is enfeeblement instead if the lassitude is the waning of a character's ability to act, measured against actions still expected.
avoided.why_not: The camera holds them as bodies in the meadow, not measured against the ship waiting; the lotus removes the wish, not the ability.

secondary.name: Fetish
secondary.question: What object has become charged?
secondary.answer: The lotus is a charged object: whoever tastes it forgets home.
secondary.operation: Insert of the lotus in a hand offered, lit warm.

avoided.name: Symptom
avoided.flip: It is Symptom instead if the object is already in the body's grip and the shot is about the act it compels (gnawing the meat, sniffing the shoe).
avoided.why_not: The shot is the fruit before the eating, not the act of devouring.

scenes.title: Goat Island and the Cyclops Coast
beats: The fleet reaches a fertile unworked island opposite the Cyclopes' land.
In darkness the ships enter a sheltered harbor and rest.
At dawn the crews hunt wild goats and feast while observing smoke and voices across the channel.
Odysseus takes one ship and selects twelve men to investigate the neighboring people.

primary.name: Originary world
primary.question: What ancient or pre-social force underlies this milieu?
primary.answer: The Cyclops coast is a land without ploughing or assembly: a pre-social ground seen across the channel.
primary.operation: Wide from Goat Island across the water: the coast, smoke rising, the voices off-screen; the men small at the fires.

avoided.name: Milieu
avoided.flip: It is Milieu instead if the place is historicised — dated architecture, social institutions, class markers laid out in establishing shots so actions exemplify a situation.
avoided.why_not: The land is not historicised; it is primal and timeless.

secondary.name: Index of lack
secondary.question: What missing situation does this action let us infer?
secondary.answer: Smoke and voices across the channel are a missing situation that Odysseus's action (one ship, twelve men) goes to fill.
secondary.operation: Odysseus's point of view on the smoke, then him choosing the men.

avoided.name: Index of equivocity
avoided.flip: It is Index of equivocity instead if the disclosure splits — the same act or clue points to two distant situations and the film refuses to settle which.
avoided.why_not: Nothing is double here; the unknown is a lack his action will fill.

scenes.title: The Empty Cave

key_beat.note: the curiosity that costs six men their lives

beats: Odysseus carries a skin of Maron's powerful wine and leads twelve men to a huge cave.
They find cheeses, pails, whey, lambs, and kids arranged by age.
The crew begs to steal food and animals and escape.
Odysseus refuses because he wants to meet the owner and receive a guest-gift.

primary.name: Index of lack
primary.question: What missing situation does this action let us infer?
primary.answer: The men read an owner's absence from what he left: racks of cheese, lambs penned by age; the searcher's eyes build the giant.
primary.operation: Slow push through the cave with the men's hands lifting a pail, touching a cheese; each object reveals the giant's scale and order.

avoided.name: Mark
avoided.flip: It is Mark/Demark instead if the revealing element is an object whose meaning comes from a habitual series being completed or broken — the thinking is done by the relation, not by the character's exploratory action.
avoided.why_not: The inference comes from their exploring, not from a series completed or broken.

secondary.name: Mark
secondary.question: What recurring thing has become meaningful because it repeats?
